Claims decision:
- Teammate's "withSession() always begins with latest" — incorrect: default first-unconstrained may route to a replica.
- Proposal's "entire session pinned to primary" — incorrect: only first query primary; later queries may use replicas. To force reads-of-own-write, pass bookmark.
- Recommended contract: write request uses withSession("first-primary") (or any session; writes always route to primary per tutorial: "Even if you use the first-unconstrained constraint or pass a bookmark, the write request will always be routed to the primary"), then persist session.getBookmark() (header/cookie) and have later request call withSession(bookmark) → read-your-own-writes across requests; fall back to first-unconstrained for purely replica-tolerant global reads. Note bookmarks only guarantee "at least as up-to-date" — not global latest.
- Batch: assumption that earlier statements remain committed is wrong: it's a SQL transaction; failure aborts/rolls back entire sequence. So run header + line items in one batch and treat failure as whole-order failure; generate idempotency/order id client-side; handle "error returned for that specific statement" per-statement results.
- Product claims: "globally latest reads" unsupported unless every read pinned to primary (first-primary only pins first query). Sequential consistency ≠ linearizability. "100 ms max replica lag after commit" — not documented; docs say replica "may be arbitrarily out of date" — UNVERIFIED/no support. Next evidence: Cloudflare support/limits for replication lag SLA.

Also: Sessions API only via Worker binding; REST not supported (#known-limitations). And note withSession works even with replication disabled.

Also failure handling: D1 query duration limit 30 s; overloaded errors; docs retry tutorial only retries specific network errors — cite tutorial step 6 for retry guidance (it retries "Network connection lost", "storage caused object to be reset", "reset because its code was updated").
